items.signal_prefix: Record June quarter: revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY)

set.signal: Record June quarter: revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.82; September-quarter guide $8.1B (+>20% QoQ). DRAM = 23% of systems revenue. DRAM technology drivers: leveraging foundry-logic capabilities into DRAM PITCH SCALING — VECTOR hard-mask and diffusion-barrier tools 'critical for next-generation requirements'; Argos surface-treatment expanding into a growing set of DRAM applications; Equipment Intelligence / Dextro self-maintaining-tool solutions now expanding from NAND INTO DRAM. HBM-relevant: advanced packaging revenue on track for >70% YoY growth on TSV etch & electroplating leadership; AI driving 'more advanced DRAM and foundry architectures' and 'larger and more complex advanced packages'.

items.reason: 'raised from >50%' comes from an analyst's question on this call (and the prior call), not from management or the deck.
items.evidence: As an industry leader in TSV etch and electroplating, we are on track to deliver greater than 70% year-on-year growth.

items.label: Lam Research Q4 FY2026 (07-29-2026)

set.signal: CALL — DRAM TO LEAD 2027 WFE: Lam expects DRAM to be the FASTEST-GROWING WFE segment in 2027 (then foundry/logic, then NAND — same order as 2026). June-quarter DRAM dollars were flattish AT THE RECORD March-quarter level (23% of systems revenue; 1-alpha/1-beta/1-gamma wafer additions + upgrades enabling DDR5/LPDDR5/HBM). Technology detail: DRAM customers adopting VECTOR hard mask for low-K film patterning (co-optimized with conductor etch; >20% COST SAVINGS vs traditional approaches) and VECTOR diffusion barriers (~5% CAPACITANCE REDUCTION vs competing tech); AKARA has won strategic tool-of-record positions including 'the most challenging GATE ETCH applications' in advanced DRAM. Thesis: 'as you try to push DRAM performance ahead, it starts to look A LOT LIKE LEADING-EDGE FOUNDRY LOGIC' — more EUV layers pull Lam's patterning etch, verticalization makes everything '3D NAND-like.' On HBM, CFO Doug Bettinger: 'as the stack gets taller, process times take longer, you need more equipment' (not quantified). Deferred revenue +$213M QoQ, the largest factor being customer down payments.

items.reason: HBM4 / HBM4E and the capital-intensity claim are the analyst's question; the CFO answered generically and declined to quantify. 'Rebound' refers to the prior quarter, not this source.
items.evidence: as the stack gets taller, process times take longer, you need more equipment, clearly we're enabling a lot of that with the things we do around the TSV. We haven't put specific numbers on it

items.label: Lam Research Q4 FY2026 (07-29-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL — WHY NAND DOUBLED AND WHAT'S NEXT

set.signal: CALL — WHY NAND DOUBLED AND WHAT'S NEXT: the demand driver is AI itself — 'expanding CONTEXT WINDOWS and PERSISTENT MEMORY requirements are driving significantly higher demand for flash storage' — with conversions to 256+ layer-class devices primarily enabling ENTERPRISE SSDs. CEO Tim Archer: 'We expect Lam Served Available Market, or SAM per wafer in NAND, to double from the 128-layer node to 500-plus layer devices' (longer process times on taller stacks + additional tool steps). Archer: 'Most of that $40 billion we had previously said would likely occur in upgrades would likely occur before the end of 2027' — and then 'it all starts again' on a BIGGER installed base as the fleet steps 200 -> 300 -> 400 -> 500+ layers (greenfield adds meanwhile enlarge the base). Asked about NAND oversupply risk: customer conversations are still about upgrading the installed base; 'fundamentals are still about the same for us'; some greenfield this year but large-scale greenfield 'a ways out.' In the 2027 WFE mix NAND is the THIRD-fastest grower behind DRAM and foundry/logic — the same order as 2026, a year Lam is outperforming in.
set.figure: NAND SAM/wafer expected 2x from 128L -> 500+L; $40B upgrades likely mostly before end-2027 then restart on bigger base; enterprise-SSD-led

items.reason: Hedges dropped ('We expect', 'would likely occur'); the TrendForce forecast is the analyst's third-party citation, not management's.
items.evidence: Most of that $40 billion we had previously said would likely occur in upgrades would likely occur before the end of 2027.

items.label: Lam Research Q4 FY2026 (07-29-2026)

set.signal: RECORD June quarter (Q4 FY2026, ended 06-28-2026): revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY) — record revenue, operating margin AND EPS; non-GAAP gross margin 52.0% (49.9% in the March quarter), operating margin 38.4%, EPS $1.82. FY2026: revenue $23.23B (+26% vs $18.44B FY2025), EPS $5.82 (vs $4.13). September-quarter guide $8.1B +/- $400M — UP >20% SEQUENTIALLY — with GM 52%, OM 39.5%, EPS $2.15. CY2026 WFE now seen in the LOW $150B RANGE (up from the $140B view last quarter); third consecutive year of WFE outperformance; CY27+ called an 'extraordinary setup' — customers have announced multi-year timelines for new fab projects. CEO Archer: 'AI-driven demand continues to reshape the semiconductor industry.' Mix: foundry 44% of systems revenue, memory 46% (DRAM 23% + NVM 23%); region Taiwan 27%, China 26%, Korea 20%. CSBG record $2.47B (+43% YoY). FCF $1.27B in Q; cash $5.6B; headcount ~22,400 (+1,800 QoQ).

items.reason: '+210bps QoQ' is the enricher's own arithmetic (52.0% minus 49.9%); both stated figures are kept instead.
items.evidence: The June quarter came in at 52%, exceeding the upper end of our guidance range and improving from the March quarter level of 49.9%.

items.label: Lam Research Q4 FY2026 (07-29-2026)

set.signal: CALL — THE 2027 WFE SETUP: 'probably eight, nine, 10 NEW FABS coming online between now and the end of next year'; the industry is 'MEANINGFULLY UNDERSUPPLIED' rolling into 2027, and customers are securing equipment orders for new clean-room space AT LEAD TIME OR BEYOND. The $140B->low-$150B CY26 WFE raise came from customers SQUEEZING OUT extra clean-room space and resolving bottleneck tools — further in-year upside is now hard, so discussions have moved to 2027 fab-fill. On sequential growth every quarter through end-2027: 'I feel incrementally good about each successive quarter.' 2027 growth order repeats 2026: DRAM fastest, foundry/logic second, NAND third. Lam is 'talking to that NEW LOGIC CUSTOMER IN THE U.S.' (unnamed). China WFE flat to slightly up — multinationals' China fabs GREW while domestic customers declined (China 26% of revenue). KEY RATIO UPDATED (CFO Doug Bettinger): the earlier '$100 billion data center CapEx equating, if I remember the number, to roughly $8 billion in WFE' was 'probably a little bit of a low estimate'; 'It's probably trending, I don't know, a billion or two higher' — hyperscale investment 'trickling all the way back to WFE.'
set.figure: 8-10 new fabs by end-2027; industry undersupplied; orders at lead time+; $100B DC capex -> ~$8B WFE, 'probably' a billion or two higher now

items.label: Lam Research Q4 FY2026 (07-29-2026)

set.signal: CALL — LONG-TERM MODEL RAISED: June-quarter gross margin 52.0% was Lam's HIGHEST IN 20 YEARS; new multi-year targets of MID-50s% GROSS MARGIN and MID-40s% OPERATING MARGIN (up from the 2025 Investor Day frame), on SAM the CFO guesses at '36%, 36.5% this year, something like that', trending to high-30s. Margin drivers: 7-country manufacturing footprint (Oregon/California/Ohio/Malaysia/Taiwan/Korea/Austria) as a strategic pricing/supply asset, annual new-product value pricing, and scale. DEMAND SIGNAL: deferred revenue rose $213M QoQ to $2.43B, the largest factor being CUSTOMER DOWN PAYMENTS. FY2026 closed with records: $23.2B revenue, 50.6% GM, EPS $5.82 (+41%). CSBG third straight record (~$2.5B, +43% YoY, record upgrades). PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING: 510mm x 515mm panel systems shipped into development programs across multiple geographies, first 310mm x 310mm tool ships this year; future AI packages seen exceeding 9x RETICLE SIZE (~3x today's mainstream) — the driver for wafer->panel transition. Capex held at 4-5% of revenue incl. major lab investments; tax rate rises to mid-teens from the September quarter.
